answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with adaptive computational admission: every new identity must solve a fresh, time-bound puzzle before it can earn, and the difficulty rises sharply when many identities appear from one inlet of requests in a short window. A lone honest agent on a small island of activity pays only a light zephyr of compute, but an attacker spawning thousands faces an exponentially growing bill in electricity, hardware time, and delay, making fake scale unprofitable before any reward is paid.
